header.name: Philosophy of Technology
header.description:
This course aims to introduce students to the basic issues and debates that arise within the philosophy of technology. These include:
1) What is Technology? How does it relate to society?
2) How do we conceive the relation between technology and science?
3) How do we understand the relationship between technology and nature?
4) Is the distinction between the ‘real’ and the ‘virtual’ still tenable?
5) Do visions of technologically dystopian or utopian futures overestimate the possibilities of technology?

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students would be able to comprehend and critically analyze key issues and debates in the philosophical thinking on technology

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: As part of their analytic comprehension students would be able to identify the historical context and its underlying presuppositions in relation to which these issues emerge.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to abstract from particular debates and be able to recognize and analyse philosophical patterns of argumentation

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Based on the capacity to abstract and recognize philosophical forms of argumentation, Students will be able to make logical and normative evaluations.

outcomes.label: CO5
outcomes.raw_text: Based on these normative evaluations students will be able to critique existing philosophical positions and suggest possible alternative approaches

lecture_topics: Topic I: Traditional Philosophical Thinking on Technology: The Alienation Thesis
Marx’s conception of the division of labour and alienation under Capitalism.
Heidegger’s articulation of the essence of technology as ‘enframing’
Topic 2: The Relation between Science and Technology
Topic 3: Social Networking and its Effects on Human Sociality
Topic 4: Environmental Crisis in the age of the ‘Anthropocene’
Disenchantment, the manipulation of nature and anthropocentric ecological arguments
Deep Ecology and the Project of ‘re-enchantment’
Dystopian and utopian views of Technological society
The possibilities and limits of technology
